# MA222 Review 2 Answers

**1.** Twelve customers at a store bought this many items each: $2,\ 3,\ 3,\ 4,\ 4,\ 4,\ 5,\ 5,\ 6,\ 3,\ 4,\ 14$. Make a dotplot of the data. Then describe the distribution: Where is the peak? What is the range? Is there an outlier?

```{=latex}
\vspace{0.45in}
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.9cm]
  \draw (-0.3,0) -- (15.3,0);
  \foreach \i in {0,...,15} { \draw (\i,0.1) -- (\i,-0.1) node[below] {\small \i}; }
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
```

```{=latex}
\vspace{\baselineskip}
```

**Answer:** Tally: 2 (1 dot), 3 (3 dots), 4 (4 dots), 5 (2 dots), 6 (1 dot), 14 (1 dot). The peak is at $4$. The range is $14 - 2 = 12$. The value $14$ is an outlier: it is far from the rest of the data.

```{=latex}
\vspace{0.45in}
```

**2.** Three student clubs have these numbers of members (no student is in more than one club):

| Club | Art | Chess | Dance |
|:--|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Members | 6 | 8 | 5 |

a) The observational units are the clubs, and the variable is the number of members in the club. Find the mean and the median of this variable. \
b) The observational units are the 19 students, and the variable is the number of members in the student's club. Find the mean and the median of this variable.

```{=latex}
\vspace{\baselineskip}
```

**Answer:** a) Mean: $\dfrac{6 + 8 + 5}{3} = \dfrac{19}{3} \approx 6.33$ members. Median: in order $5, 6, 8$, so $6$ members. b) Six students report 6, eight report 8, and five report 5. Mean: $\dfrac{6 \cdot 6 + 8 \cdot 8 + 5 \cdot 5}{19} = \dfrac{36 + 64 + 25}{19} = \dfrac{125}{19} \approx 6.58$ members. Median: in order, five 5s, six 6s, then eight 8s; the middle (10th) of the 19 values is $6$ members.

```{=latex}
\vspace{0.45in}
```

**3.** Maya and Leo take exams in different classes.

| | Score | Class mean | Class std dev |
|:--|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Maya | $88$ | $80$ | $6$ |
| Leo | $91$ | $85$ | $4$ |

Who did better compared to their own class? Use z-values to explain.

```{=latex}
\vspace{\baselineskip}
```

**Answer:** Maya: $z = \dfrac{88 - 80}{6} = \dfrac{8}{6} = 1.33$. Leo: $z = \dfrac{91 - 85}{4} = \dfrac{6}{4} = 1.5$. Leo did better compared to his class: he is $1.5$ standard deviations above his class mean, and Maya is $1.33$ above hers.

```{=latex}
\vspace{0.45in}
```

**4.** Use the standard normal table. Sketch the area, then find the left tail area for $z = -1.47$.

```{=latex}
\vspace{\baselineskip}
```

**Answer:** Row $-1.4$, column $.07$: left tail area $= 0.0708 \approx 7\%$.

```{=latex}
\vspace{0.45in}
```

**5.** Use the standard normal table. Sketch the area, then find the right tail area for $z = 1.21$.

```{=latex}
\vspace{\baselineskip}
```

**Answer:** Row $1.2$, column $.01$: left tail area $= 0.8869$, so right tail area $= 1.0 - 0.8869 = 0.1131 \approx 11\%$.

```{=latex}
\vspace{0.45in}
```

**6.** Use the standard normal table. Sketch the area, then find the area between $z = -0.85$ and $z = 1.10$.

```{=latex}
\vspace{\baselineskip}
```

**Answer:** Left tail area for $z = 1.10$ (row $1.1$, column $.00$) is $0.8643$. Left tail area for $z = -0.85$ (row $-0.8$, column $.05$) is $0.1977$. Area between $= 0.8643 - 0.1977 = 0.6666 \approx 67\%$.

```{=latex}
\vspace{0.45in}
```
